topic_summary: Analysis of the King James Version (KJV) Bible as a contested kernel where different interpretive traditions read the same fixed text as either exclusively divinely inspired (KJV-Only movement) or as a historically situated, revisable translation (mainline/academic traditions). The readings instantiate fundamentally different constraints on biblical authority, translation validity, and who holds legitimate power to adjudicate religious practice.

key_entities: King James Version 1611 text (the stabilized kernel)
KJV-Only movement (interpretive authority claiming exclusive inspiration)
Mainline Protestant denominations (interpretive authority grounded in scholarly revision)
Earlier manuscript traditions (Textus Receptus, Masoretic Text, Dead Sea Scrolls)
key_tensions: Divine inspiration vs human translation (ontological status of KJV text)
Fixity as fidelity vs fixity as fossilization (interpretive legitimacy grounding)
key_mechanisms: Doctrine of verbal plenary inspiration (mechanism grounding KJV-Only authority)
Manuscript comparison/eclectic text method (mechanism grounding academic authority)
key_absences: Economic incentives (KJV public domain vs modern translations under copyright)
Demographic distribution (KJV-Only concentrated in independent fundamentalist churches)
Translation history (KJV itself revised earlier English translations; historical revisability obscured)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The King James Version (1611) as a fixed, codified English biblical text claimed as the authoritative transmission of divine revelation
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested between KJV-Only movement (authority derived from claimed divine preservation of this specific translation) and mainline/academic traditions (authority derived from scholarly consensus and manuscript evidence)

readings.commitment: The KJV is the exclusively inspired, inerrant English Bible; all other translations are corrupted or inferior
readings.authority_grounding: Divine preservation doctrine — God supernaturally preserved the Textus Receptus lineage and the KJV translation process
readings.expected_structural_delta: Modern translations enter victim set (suppressed as illegitimate); KJV-Only leadership becomes sole arbiter of textual authority; high extractiveness via gate-keeping of 'true' scripture

readings.commitment: The KJV is a historically important but improvable translation; better manuscripts and linguistic knowledge justify revision
readings.authority_grounding: Scholarly consensus via textual criticism — authority derived from manuscript evidence and academic peer review
readings.expected_structural_delta: Translation selection becomes consumer choice (low suppression); academic scholars become arbiters; extractiveness shifts to publishing industry control of modern translations

readings.commitment: Multiple translations serve complementary purposes; KJV valuable for literary/historical reasons, modern versions for clarity
readings.authority_grounding: Pragmatic pluralism — authority distributed across translation committees and denominational endorsement
readings.expected_structural_delta: No single text holds gate-keeping power; extractiveness reduced but coordination costs increase; authority decentralized

axiom_contradictions.basis: Exclusive inspiration requires that translation process itself was divinely guided and thus unrevisable; revisable translation requires that all translations (including KJV) are human products subject to error and improvement. No coherent framework holds both: accepting divine preservation of KJV translation requires rejecting the claim that better manuscripts justify revision.

Exclusive inspiration requires one uniquely authoritative text; functional equivalence requires that authority can be distributed across multiple valid translations. No coherent framework holds both: accepting KJV as exclusively inspired requires rejecting the legitimacy of treating modern translations as equally valid for any purpose.
